subject: Re: Mosaic — MSA/order form redlines: output rights & training opt-out
messages:
From: Jessica Smith <jessica.smith@mosaichealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mosaichealth.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — data use & derivative rights

Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal/procurement teams reviewed the MSA and attached order form and flagged a few items we need clarified before we proceed to signature. The main concern is the language that appears to grant Redwood rights to use customer content for model training and broad ownership claims over "derivative" outputs. For Mosaic Health, PHI-adjacent data and downstream productization are sensitive — we need explicit limits.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood asserts ownership of outputs produced by our prompts or claims any title to downstream products.
- Confirm that Redwood will not use our content to train models without explicit opt-in.
- Provide evidence or reference to your telemetry/data retention policy for requests logged by the hosted API.

I've attached our redline (Mosaic_Redlines_20260803.pdf) with suggested edits. Can we get a counterproposal from legal that preserves basic telemetry for debugging but removes training-by-default language? We are targeting a purchase order by 8/16, so a quick back-and-forth this week would be ideal.

Appreciate it — feel free to loop in legal.

--
Jessica Smith
Director, Procurement
Mosaic Health
attachments: Mosaic_Redlines_20260803.pdf

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Smith <jessica.smith@mosaichealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — data use & derivative rights

Jessica — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Looping legal (Laura) and our solutions lead (Ben) so we can put together precise counter language and an evidence packet.

High level from me: we do not want to block operational telemetry (errors, latency metrics) used to run and improve the service, but we can be explicit that customer prompts/outputs won't be used to train public models without customer opt-in. My ask to legal: propose an MSA/Order Form carveout that:
- Grants Mosaic a perpetual, worldwide license to outputs for productization (customer can do as they please).
- Restricts Redwood from training on customer content unless Mosaic opts in via the Order Form or a signed training addendum.
- Allows aggregated telemetry for quality/improvements, with a clear retention window and removal process.

I'll compile a short redline summary and send it back; appreciate Laura's eyeballs on acceptable wording and evidence we can share for procurement (audit logs, retention controls).

Quick note: procurement timeline looks tight — can we aim to exchange counter-redlines by EOD tomorrow? I can host a 30-min sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0194
attachments: redline_summary_20260803.txt

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jessica Smith <jessica.smith@mosaichealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — proposed counterlanguage and evidence list

Team / Jessica — reviewing the Mosaic redline now. Below are proposed approaches and the evidence packet we can provide to procurement. I tried to keep the customer-facing language concise and procurement-friendly.

1) Proposed MSA/Order Form language (high level)
- Output license: "Subject to payment of fees, Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable right to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute any output generated by the Service in Customer's Products and Services."
- Training: "Provider will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or improve any public model, or include such data in model training datasets, without Customer's prior written consent. The Order Form may include an explicit opt-in box for training consent."
- Telemetry/ops data: "Provider may collect aggregated, de-identified telemetry for operational purposes; such telemetry will not contain Customer Content or Outputs and will be retained for no longer than 90 days unless otherwise agreed."

2) Evidence we can share with Mosaic procurement
- SOC 2 summary and control mapping (redacted): confirms logging practices and access controls.
- Data retention & deletion playbook (ops runbook) — summarizes 90-day retention and deletion requests.
- Sample audit log extract showing request-level metadata (no prompt/output payloads) — useful to show what we share for debugging.
- Proposed DPA / training addendum template that explicitly requires customer opt-in.

3) Redline mechanics & next steps
- I've prepared a short counter redline (attached: MSA_counter_redline_20260804.docx) that implements the clauses above and removes any ambiguous "ownership" phrasing in the Order Form. Key points to watch: be explicit about "Outputs" vs "Customer Content"; avoid assignment wording that looks like title transfer of customer outputs to Provider.
- If Mosaic is okay with the draft, we can attach a one-line training opt-in checkbox to the Order Form and surface the DPA for signature alongside the PO.

Action items:
- Dylan: please propose a 30-min window for a legal/procurement sync today or tomorrow; I can make time.
- Ben: please prepare an ops packet with the SOC 2 extract and the retention playbook for Jessica.
- Jessica: flag any language in the counter that doesn't meet Mosaic's regulatory needs (HIPAA/PHI constraints).

Happy to discuss on a call.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_counter_redline_20260804.docx

From: Jessica Smith <jessica.smith@mosaichealth.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — agreed-on approach and next steps

Laura / Dylan — thanks, that language is much closer to what Mosaic needs. Two small asks before we proceed:

1) In the telemetry clause, can you replace "de-identified" with "aggregated and anonymized" and confirm the 90-day retention window applies to request-level logs used for debugging (we need assurance that payloads are purged).
2) Would you provide the SOC 2 mapping and a sample redacted audit log extract so our compliance team can validate controls? A DocuSign package with the Order Form + DPA would speed sign-off.

If you can share the attachments and a DocuSign link today, we can route for approval — I expect procurement sign-off within 3 business days after that. Also happy to take a 30-min call tomorrow (8/5) 10:00–10:30 PT to walk legal/procurement through the revised clauses.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Jessica
Director, Procurement
Mosaic Health
